description.value: X2 EDU is a distinct X2 configuration in the manufacturer brochure. EDU is a 29-DOF, 35 kg research/assembly platform with seven DOF per arm. Its 130 cm height includes the dummy head. RK3588 compute, motion-control interfaces and configurable sensor/compute expansion support development. The 1.8 m/s maximum and two-hour 500 Wh endurance remain EDU-specific. Assembly/disassembly and component-kit procurement are explicit use cases. Optional grippers, dummy hands and fists are not an included fully dexterous hand.

description.value: Codey Rocky combines the programmable Codey electronics with the mobile Rocky base. Its manufacturer getting-started tutorial describes more than ten programmable electronic modules, block and Python programming in mBlock 5, and movement exercises including line following and obstacle response. The handbook recommends ages six and older with adult accompaniment and specifies a 5 V/1 A charging adapter without a charging duration. The Spring 2022 catalog describes Wi-Fi/Bluetooth and distinguishes single and education packs. Numeric mass, runtime, current price and first-release year remain unverified here.

The article planned a CES 2026 debut and phased production from March 2026; the old plan is not proof that production, delivery or final specifications occurred. An unnamed surgical column in the catalog is not assigned to EIR.

The SDK exposes camera, proximity/touch sensing, facial recognition/enrollment, expressive animation and text-to-speech. Those API limits are not body dimensions, payload or guaranteed docking performance. description.value: DriveMod Tugger is Cyngn’s autonomous integration of a Motrec MT-160 tow tractor. Current developer specifications describe the 12,000 lb towing configuration with a separately rated 500 lb deck load, 65 × 30 × 55 in dimensions and 1,250 ± 100 lb mass depending on options. Maximum travel is 4 mph autonomous or 6 mph manual; battery operation is up to twelve hours depending on load/speed/usage, with five-hour charging and an unspecified charge window. Current turning radius is 53 in, minimum aisle 59 in and maximum grade 2.5 percent. The October 2023 preview’s 6,000 lb/54 in figures predate a documented 2024 upgrade. 3D-LiDAR mapping, FMS dispatch, manual override and redundant stop functions support site-specific workflows. Auto-unhitch and LTE retain attachment/optional scope; no blanket whole-system certification or guaranteed ROI is established.

description.value: Ekso Indego Therapy is the separately named adjustable clinical lower-limb exoskeleton. The current site places it under Past Products, whereas the issuer’s February 23, 2026 report described product sales; this does not prove current new-device supply or cessation of support. Clinical US safety 043-016-001.A lists 39 lbf/17.7 kgf as printed device weight, 72.8 × 46.3 × 57.6 cm, four-hour operating time and four-hour charging. Wearer fitting and less-than-five-minute setup are separate from device geometry and standardized throughput. The clinical manual excludes home/community use, sports and stairs; Personal specifications are not inherited.

description.value: GR100 is Running Brains Robotics’ outdoor patrol and inspection robot, explicitly launched in 2021 in the company history. The product page gives 157 kg mass, maximum 1.5 m/s travel speed, 4.5 h autonomy and 1.5 h fast charging at a stated 1000 W, without a defined charging state-of-charge window. description.value: Tally RFID is the named RFID-enabled Tally sensing configuration, announced on July 18, 2018 as integration of RFID and machine learning with computer vision. The current product page claims up to 120,000 items in 3 h and up to 750 tag reads/s. It gives conflicting range text: headline up to 35 ft and body up to 40 ft; the configuration or test basis is unresolved. RFID reading distance is not navigation accuracy or a guaranteed all-item detection radius. The 2018 release’s over-700-tags/s and sub-meter product-location claims retain their historical scope. RAIN/GS1 standards wording is an attributed supplier claim. Current Tally 4.0 battery/mass and fixed-camera Tally Spot specifications are not inherited.

description.value: AmbiSort A-Series is Ambi Robotics’ configurable small-parcel sorting system for sacks or totes. A soft-touch gripper transfers parcels across four barcode scanners and two quality-control zones to a gantry; operators seal and replace full sacks. The current configurator’s 66 destinations is explicitly a mock placeholder, while an older Q3 2022 deck describes 66 sacks for a particular historical customer layout and names an A-Series v2 schematic. A November 2024 manufacturer case report gives 355 sorts/h in 2022, 410 in 2023 and 500 after 2024 upgrades, with 99.6% sort accuracy in the latter context. These dated customer figures are not a guaranteed current rating or dimensional vision precision. Generic AmbiSort 2020 production does not establish this named generation’s first release.

description.value: AmbiStack is Ambi Robotics’ configurable overhead stacking system, publicly introduced January 28, 2025. The current FAQ permits cases up to 50 lb each and 52×32×32 in; those are handled-case limits, not robot mass, dimensions or aggregate multi-pick capacity. It supports mixed/SKU-based palletizing and multiple output formats, with 6/12/more positions as layout choices. Sim2Real planning and vision support two-case multipicking, while operators or separate AMRs/AGVs remove completed pallets. Light-curtain zones let a gantry work on one half while the other is replenished. A June 30, 2026 company release reports integration with Pickle Robot’s separate truck-unloading machines; 2025 deployment targets and current complete-system price/stock remain distinct.

description.value: AmbiSort B-Series is Ambi Robotics’ modular induction and sorting system, introduced June 6, 2023. Robot arms use multi-suction parcel grasping, a central conveyor and six-sided scanning to route to configured containers or exception outputs. Input, outputs, arm count and layout are configuration choices; operators replenish full containers.

description.value: BOTONY is Greenfield Robotics' autonomous agricultural robot for chemical-free mechanical weed control in broadacre crops such as soybeans, milo, cotton and corn. The manufacturer offers wheeled and tracked configurations and estimates approximately 7 acres per day per robot under optimal conditions. Cutting is optimally initiated when weeds reach 3–5 inches, with a specified 60-inch turn zone. Each robot uses the GreenTRIP RTK system for field mapping and autonomous navigation with a 15 km range radius and centimeter-level accuracy, onboard cameras with human-detection algorithms and geofencing, and the Operator software for remote monitoring and intervention. The company reports a 2025 leased fleet of 23 robots in seven states and 70 orders for 2026 delivery, and operates made-to-order without maintaining robot inventory.

description.value: ANAFI UKR is Parrot's compact folding micro-UAV for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance missions. The manufacturer lists a folded size of 245 x 160 x 116 mm, a mass below 1,033 g with the Standard Smart battery or below 1,365 g with the XLR battery, and a 1,450 g maximum take-off mass. Flight time is 38 minutes with the Standard battery at 6 m/s or 70 minutes with the XLR battery at 6.5 m/s; maximum flight distance is 23 km or 40 km respectively. The aircraft reaches 17 m/s maximum horizontal airspeed, 8 m/s ascent and descent, resists 15 m/s wind and is rated IP53. It combines a 640 thermal sensor with wide and telephoto EO sensors on a 3-axis stabilized gimbal, uses GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou plus optical navigation for GNSS-denied flight, and can take off from and land in the operator's hand. description.value: temi V3 is Robotemi's autonomous indoor personal assistant and telepresence robot. It stands 100 cm tall, is 35 cm wide and 45 cm deep, and weighs 12 kg. A 13.3-inch 1920 x 1080 IPS touch display tilts from -15 to +55 degrees, and the robot runs on an ARM hexa-core platform with Linux and a separate navigation computer. Navigation combines 360-degree LiDAR, two depth cameras, an RGB camera, an IMU and six time-of-flight linear sensors for 2D mapping, 3D localization and 5 cm / 2 inch accuracy, with obstacle avoidance, user detection and following. The lithium-ion battery provides up to eight hours of operation per charge and the robot returns autonomously to its charging dock. It offers Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.1 BLE, USB-C and USB-A, optional 4G/5G, a 13 MP 1080p camera, four microphones and 20 W audio. The tray carries up to 3 kg depending on assembly. Robotemi publishes no numeric price or IP rating.

description.value: The Lucid Gravity Robotaxi is a purpose-built autonomous ride-hailing vehicle developed by Lucid, Nuro and Uber. It is based on Lucid’s all-electric Gravity SUV and uses the Nuro Driver with a 360-degree sensor array of high-resolution cameras, lidar and radars integrated into the body and a roof-mounted Halo module. description.value: The Mammotion LUBA 3 AWD 1500 is a wire-free all-wheel-drive mower for lawns up to 0.37 acre. Mammotion publishes an 80% (38.6°) slope rating, a 15 Ah battery for 215 min per charge, 41 lbs mass, IPX6, 70 dB or less noise, 1.0-2.7 in standard or 2.2-4.0 in high cutting height and 0.37, 0.75 or 1.25 acre coverage for the 1500, 3000 and 5000. It handles 300+ obstacles, 100 mowing zones, DropMow, anti-fall and lift detection, 70 cm gaps and up to 10 cloud-backed maps. The reviewed page publishes no charging time, cutting width or area rate.
